From 6c5a9baa15de240e747263aba435a0951da8d8d2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Mehul Rao <mehulrao@gmail.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 13:07:30 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] tipc: fix divide-by-zero in tipc_sk_filter_connect()

A user can set conn_timeout to any value via
setsockopt(TIPC_CONN_TIMEOUT), including values less than 4.  When a
SYN is rejected with TIPC_ERR_OVERLOAD and the retry path in
tipc_sk_filter_connect() executes:

    delay %= (tsk->conn_timeout / 4);

If conn_timeout is in the range [0, 3], the integer division yields 0,
and the modulo operation triggers a divide-by-zero exception, causing a
kernel oops/panic.

Fix this by clamping conn_timeout to a minimum of 4 at the point of use
in tipc_sk_filter_connect().

Oops: divide error: 0000 [#1] SMP KASAN NOPTI
CPU: 0 UID: 0 PID: 119 Comm: poc-F144 Not tainted 7.0.0-rc2+
RIP: 0010:tipc_sk_filter_rcv (net/tipc/socket.c:2236 net/tipc/socket.c:2362)
Call Trace:
 tipc_sk_backlog_rcv (include/linux/instrumented.h:82 include/linux/atomic/atomic-instrumented.h:32 include/net/sock.h:2357 net/tipc/socket.c:2406)
 __release_sock (include/net/sock.h:1185 net/core/sock.c:3213)
 release_sock (net/core/sock.c:3797)
 tipc_connect (net/tipc/socket.c:2570)
 __sys_connect (include/linux/file.h:62 include/linux/file.h:83 net/socket.c:2098)

Fixes: 6787927475e5 ("tipc: buffer overflow handling in listener socket")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Mehul Rao <mehulrao@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Tung Nguyen <tung.quang.nguyen@est.tech>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260310170730.28841-1-mehulrao@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/tipc/socket.c b/net/tipc/socket.c
index 4c618c2b871d..9329919fb07f 100644
--- a/net/tipc/socket.c
+++ b/net/tipc/socket.c
@@ -2233,6 +2233,8 @@ static bool tipc_sk_filter_connect(struct tipc_sock *tsk, struct sk_buff *skb,
 		if (skb_queue_empty(&sk->sk_write_queue))
 			break;
 		get_random_bytes(&delay, 2);
+		if (tsk->conn_timeout < 4)
+			tsk->conn_timeout = 4;
 		delay %= (tsk->conn_timeout / 4);
 		delay = msecs_to_jiffies(delay + 100);
 		sk_reset_timer(sk, &sk->sk_timer, jiffies + delay);
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch

The patch fixes a divide-by-zero vulnerability in the TIPC (Transparent Inter-Process Communication) socket layer. The issue occurs in the `tipc_sk_filter_connect()` function when a user sets a very small `conn_timeout` value (less than 4) via `setsockopt(TIPC_CONN_TIMEOUT)`. During a retry path after a SYN rejection, the code performs a modulo operation using `conn_timeout / 4`. If `conn_timeout` is 0–3, the division yields zero, causing a division-by-zero exception and a kernel crash.

### Modifications per file

**net/tipc/socket.c** (single file change)  
- Added a safety check before the division: if `tsk->conn_timeout` is less than 4, it is clamped to the minimum value of 4. This ensures the subsequent division `tsk->conn_timeout / 4` always produces a non-zero divisor, preventing the divide-by-zero.

### Relationship between modifications

The change is self-contained within one file and directly addresses the root cause. By enforcing a lower bound on `conn_timeout` right before its risky use (the modulo operation), the patch eliminates the possibility of a zero divisor while preserving the intended retry delay logic. No other parts of the code are affected.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>delay %= (tsk->conn_timeout / 4);</text>
Reason:
The conn_timeout socket option can be set to a value less than 4 by the user via setsockopt(TIPC_CONN_TIMEOUT). When the retry path executes this line after a SYN rejection with TIPC_ERR_OVERLOAD, the integer division yields 0 if conn_timeout is in [0,3], causing a divide-by-zero exception.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (tsk->conn_timeout < 4)</text>
<text>	tsk->conn_timeout = 4;</text>
Reason:
This clamp ensures that conn_timeout is at least 4 before the division, preventing the denominator from being zero and thus avoiding the divide-by-zero panic.
